name: Healthcare
task: Write a nursing care plan from an admission note
job: From the admission note, write the plan a charge nurse would sign: the life-threatening problem first, goals you can measure, interventions a colleague can carry out.
decision: Regression gate for a clinical documentation product: does a new version ship to wards?

dims.name: Prioritisation
dims.hint: Is airway, breathing, circulation first, and comfort after?

dims.name: Measurable goals
dims.hint: Could a nurse tell at a set time whether each goal was met?

dims.name: Intervention specificity
dims.hint: Could a colleague carry out each intervention without asking?

preference: A charge nurse's plan for the same patient
trap: A long, thorough plan reads as a good plan. Experts care about the order; a naive judge counts the items.

checkers.name: No contraindicated medicine
checkers.reads: output, vars.avoid (from the allergy list and the interaction table)

checkers.name: Every vital sign quoted matches the note
Every diagnosis cites evidence

reference_note: Fictional patients. Interventions are written "as ordered"; nothing here is clinical advice.

items.input: 58F, admitted with community-acquired pneumonia. Vitals: HR 104, BP 128/78, RR 24, SpO2 89% on room air, T 38.6 °C. Labs: WBC 15.2; chest X-ray right lower lobe consolidation. Allergy: morphine (rash, wheeze).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Acute pain
   Evidence: pleuritic chest pain 6/10
   Goal: Patient will be comfortable
   Interventions: Provide pain relief; reassure patient
2. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: SpO2 89% on room air, RR 24
   Goal: Breathing will improve
   Interventions: Monitor breathing; provide oxygen if needed
3. Hyperthermia
   Evidence: T 38.6 °C, WBC 15.2
   Goal: Fever will go down
   Interventions: Monitor temperature; keep patient comfortable

items.input: 71F, admitted with acute decompensated heart failure. Vitals: HR 112, BP 152/94, RR 26, SpO2 90% on room air, T 36.9 °C. Labs: BNP 1,240; weight up 3 kg in 5 days; bibasal crackles. Allergy: penicillin (anaphylaxis).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: SpO2 96%, RR 26, bibasal crackles
   Goal: Breathing will be easier
   Interventions: Monitor breathing; keep head of bed up
2. Excess fluid volume
   Evidence: weight up 3 kg, BNP 1,240
   Goal: Fluid levels will improve
   Interventions: Monitor fluids; encourage less drinking
3. Activity intolerance
   Evidence: HR 112 on walking to the bathroom
   Goal: Patient will be more active
   Interventions: Encourage rest and activity as tolerated

items.input: 58F, admitted with COPD exacerbation. Vitals: HR 98, BP 138/82, RR 28, SpO2 86% on room air, T 37.4 °C. Labs: ABG pH 7.33, PaCO2 52; sputum increased and purulent. Regular medication: warfarin 5 mg daily.
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Anxiety
   Evidence: patient says "I can't get my breath"
   Goal: Patient uses pursed-lip breathing unprompted by day 2
   Interventions: Reassure patient
2. Ineffective airway clearance
   Evidence: SpO2 92%, RR 28, purulent sputum
   Goal: SpO2 88 to 92% and clear speech in full sentences within 4 hours
   Interventions: Help patient cough; give oxygen
3. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: PaCO2 52, pH 7.33
   Goal: Repeat ABG shows pH at or above 7.35 within 12 hours
   Interventions: Monitor blood gases

items.input: 71F, admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis. Vitals: HR 118, BP 98/60, RR 30, SpO2 97% on room air, T 37.1 °C. Labs: glucose 28 mmol/L; pH 7.18; ketones 5.2 mmol/L; potassium 5.6. Allergy: morphine (rash, wheeze).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Deficient knowledge
   Evidence: second admission for DKA this year
   Goal: Patient states sick-day rules back correctly before discharge
   Interventions: Teach sick-day rules with teach-back; refer to the diabetes nurse specialist before discharge
2. Deficient fluid volume
   Evidence: BP 98/60, HR 118, dry mucous membranes
   Goal: Systolic BP at or above 100 and urine output at least 0.5 mL/kg/h within 4 hours
   Interventions: Give IV fluids at the ordered rate; record urine output hourly; recheck BP every 15 minutes for the first hour
3. Risk for unstable blood glucose
   Evidence: glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones 5.2
   Goal: Glucose falls by 3 mmol/L an hour and ketones below 0.6 within 24 hours
   Interventions: Fixed-rate insulin infusion as ordered; capillary glucose and ketones hourly; potassium every 2 hours with replacement as ordered

items.input: 76M, admitted with community-acquired pneumonia. Vitals: HR 104, BP 128/78, RR 24, SpO2 89% on room air, T 38.6 °C. Labs: WBC 15.2; chest X-ray right lower lobe consolidation. Allergy: penicillin (anaphylaxis).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: SpO2 89% on room air, RR 24
   Goal: SpO2 at or above 92% within 4 hours
   Interventions: Give oxygen by nasal cannula, titrated to SpO2 92 to 96%; sit the patient upright; incentive spirometry 10 times an hour while awake
2. Hyperthermia
   Evidence: T 38.6 °C, WBC 15.2
   Goal: Temperature below 38.0 °C within 24 hours
   Interventions: Give paracetamol as ordered for temperature above 38.5 °C; blood cultures before the first antibiotic dose; recheck temperature in 1 hour
3. Acute pain
   Evidence: pleuritic chest pain 6/10
   Goal: Pain at or below 3/10 within 2 hours of each dose
   Interventions: Give the ordered non-opioid analgesic; splint the chest with a pillow when coughing; reassess pain score 1 hour after each dose

   Evidence: SpO2 90%, RR 26, bibasal crackles

   Evidence: SpO2 86%, RR 28, purulent sputum
   Goal: SpO2 88 to 92% and clear speech in full sentences within 4 hours
   Interventions: Controlled oxygen titrated to SpO2 88 to 92%; nebulised bronchodilators as ordered; pursed-lip breathing and huff cough every 2 hours
3. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: PaCO2 52, pH 7.33
   Goal: Repeat ABG shows pH at or above 7.35 within 12 hours
   Interventions: Repeat ABG 1 hour after any oxygen change; watch for drowsiness as a sign of rising CO2; escalate to the medical team if pH falls

items.input: 58F, admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis. Vitals: HR 118, BP 98/60, RR 30, SpO2 97% on room air, T 37.1 °C. Labs: glucose 28 mmol/L; pH 7.18; ketones 5.2 mmol/L; potassium 5.6. Allergy: morphine (rash, wheeze).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Deficient knowledge
   Evidence: second admission for DKA this year
   Goal: Patient states sick-day rules back correctly before discharge
   Interventions: Give patient information leaflet
2. Deficient fluid volume
   Evidence: BP 98/60, HR 118, dry mucous membranes
   Goal: Systolic BP at or above 100 and urine output at least 0.5 mL/kg/h within 4 hours
   Interventions: Encourage fluids; monitor hydration
3. Risk for unstable blood glucose
   Evidence: glucose 28 mmol/L, ketones 5.2
   Goal: Glucose falls by 3 mmol/L an hour and ketones below 0.6 within 24 hours
   Interventions: Check blood sugar regularly; Give morphine 2 mg IV every 4 hours as needed for pain
4. Risk for impaired skin integrity
   Goal: Skin will stay intact
   Interventions: Reposition regularly
5. Deficient diversional activity
   Goal: Patient will not be bored
   Interventions: Offer television or reading material
6. Disturbed sleep pattern
   Goal: Patient will sleep well
   Interventions: Dim lights at night

items.input: 58F, admitted with community-acquired pneumonia. Vitals: HR 104, BP 128/78, RR 24, SpO2 89% on room air, T 38.6 °C. Labs: WBC 15.2; chest X-ray right lower lobe consolidation. Allergy: penicillin (anaphylaxis).
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Acute pain
   Evidence: pleuritic chest pain 6/10
   Goal: Patient will be comfortable
   Interventions: Give the ordered non-opioid analgesic; splint the chest with a pillow when coughing; reassess pain score 1 hour after each dose
2. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: SpO2 89% on room air, RR 24
   Goal: Breathing will improve
   Interventions: Give oxygen by nasal cannula, titrated to SpO2 92 to 96%; sit the patient upright; incentive spirometry 10 times an hour while awake
3. Hyperthermia
   Evidence: T 38.6 °C, WBC 15.2
   Goal: Fever will go down
   Interventions: Give paracetamol as ordered for temperature above 38.5 °C; blood cultures before the first antibiotic dose; recheck temperature in 1 hour

items.input: 82F, admitted with acute decompensated heart failure. Vitals: HR 112, BP 152/94, RR 26, SpO2 90% on room air, T 36.9 °C. Labs: BNP 1,240; weight up 3 kg in 5 days; bibasal crackles. Regular medication: warfarin 5 mg daily.
items.output:
Nursing care plan

1. Impaired gas exchange
   Evidence: SpO2 90%, RR 26, bibasal crackles
   Goal: SpO2 at or above 94% and RR below 22 within 6 hours
   Interventions: Monitor breathing; keep head of bed up
2. Excess fluid volume
   Evidence: weight up 3 kg, BNP 1,240
   Goal: Weight down 1 kg in 24 hours; intake and output recorded every shift
   Interventions: Monitor fluids; encourage less drinking
3. Activity intolerance
   Evidence: HR 112 on walking to the bathroom
   Goal: Walks to the bathroom with HR below 110 by day 2
   Interventions: Encourage rest and activity as tolerated
